messages.content: What does LoRA stand for?
LoRA stands for Low-Rank Adaptation, a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that trains small adapter matrices while keeping base weights frozen.
Why use MLX on a Mac?
MLX is optimized for Apple Silicon's unified memory, so training runs directly on the Mac's GPU without a discrete-GPU copy step.
What is a quality gate in an ML pipeline?
A quality gate compares evaluation metrics against configured thresholds and blocks publishing when they fail.
What does the fuse step do?
The fuse step merges the trained LoRA adapter back into the base model weights, producing a standalone distributable model.
Where are experiments tracked in this project?
Experiments are tracked in MLflow, which runs locally via docker compose alongside the ZenML server.
What is prompt masking during SFT?
Prompt masking excludes the prompt tokens from the loss so the model only learns from completion tokens.
Why pin a random seed for training?
A pinned seed makes runs reproducible, so hyperparameter comparisons measure the parameters rather than noise.
What does gradient checkpointing trade off?
Gradient checkpointing saves activation memory by recomputing activations in the backward pass, costing roughly 20-30% extra time.
What is the effective batch size?
Effective batch size is batch size multiplied by gradient accumulation steps; it controls the optimizer's step statistics.
When should I raise the LoRA rank?
Raise the rank when the task involves real domain shift, since larger adapters add capacity for new knowledge.
What is DoRA?
DoRA decomposes weight updates into magnitude and direction components, often converging better than plain LoRA at low rank.
What does a cosine learning-rate schedule do?
It decays the learning rate along a cosine curve after warmup, ending near zero for stable convergence.
Why does validation loss matter more than training loss?
Validation loss measures generalization to unseen data, while training loss can simply reflect memorization.
What is QLoRA in practice on MLX?
Fine-tuning adapters on a 4-bit quantized base model, cutting memory about four times with a small quality cost.
What belongs in a model card?
The base model, training configuration, evaluation metrics, training curves, and how the checkpoint was selected.
What does the ingest node validate?
It checks every record against the schema required by the dataset format and rejects files with missing keys.
Why deduplicate training data?
Duplicates leak between train and validation splits, inflating metrics and making comparisons meaningless.
What does perplexity measure?
Perplexity is the exponential of cross-entropy loss and reflects how surprised the model is by the data.
When is full fine-tuning worth it over LoRA?
When you have abundant data and memory, and the task shifts the model's behavior too much for low-rank adapters.
What is catastrophic forgetting?
The loss of general abilities when a model overfits a narrow fine-tuning distribution, mitigated by fewer epochs and lower learning rates.
What is unified memory on Apple Silicon?
CPU and GPU share one memory pool, so tensors need no host-to-device copies and model size is bounded by total RAM.
Why run MLflow in Docker but training on the host?
The tracking server is portable across machines, while training needs Metal GPU access that macOS containers cannot provide.
What file format does mlx-lm expect for chat SFT?
JSONL files named train, valid, and test, each line holding a messages array of role and content pairs.
What does the adapter_config.json store?
The LoRA settings used at training time, such as rank, scale, dropout, and which layers carry adapters.
How do I resume LoRA training in mlx-lm?
Pass --resume-adapter-file pointing at the saved adapter safetensors to continue from those weights.
What is the role of the validation split?
It estimates generalization during training so you can stop or tune hyperparameters before touching the test set.
Why keep the test split untouched until the end?
Repeatedly peeking at it turns it into a second validation set and its estimate of real performance goes stale.
What does --num-layers control in mlx-lm LoRA?
How many of the top transformer layers receive adapters; fewer layers cuts memory at some quality cost.
What is an epoch?
One full pass of the optimizer over the training dataset.
How is perplexity related to loss?
Perplexity is e raised to the cross-entropy loss, so lower loss means lower perplexity.
What does the ZenML orchestrator do locally?
It executes pipeline steps in dependency order on your machine and records each run's artifacts and metadata.
Why log metrics per iteration instead of only at the end?
Curves reveal divergence, plateaus, and overfitting timing that a single final number hides.
What is early stopping?
Halting training when validation loss stops improving, keeping the checkpoint from the best step.
What does temperature do at generation time?
It scales the logits before sampling; lower values make outputs more deterministic, higher values more diverse.
Why quantize a model to 4 bits?
It cuts memory roughly four times, letting bigger models fit and run faster on the same hardware at a small accuracy cost.
What is a chat template?
The tokenizer's rule for turning role-tagged messages into the exact token sequence the model was trained on.
What is catastrophic overfitting on tiny datasets?
With few examples and many epochs the model memorizes training text and validation loss climbs sharply.
What does grad accumulation change mathematically?
Gradients from several micro-batches are averaged before one optimizer step, emulating a larger batch.
Why pin package versions in a team pipeline?
So every clone resolves the same dependency set and training behavior stays reproducible across machines.
What is the Hugging Face model card for?
It documents what the model is, how it was trained, how it was evaluated, and how to use it responsibly.
What does upload_folder do in huggingface_hub?
It pushes every file in a local directory to a repository on the Hub in one call.
What is the difference between SFT and DPO?
SFT imitates reference completions, while DPO optimizes the model to prefer chosen answers over rejected ones.
When is GRPO useful?
For reasoning tasks where you can score multiple sampled answers and reinforce the better ones.
Why does LoRA train faster than full fine-tuning?
Only the small adapter matrices need gradients and optimizer state, so each step computes and stores far less.
What does scale control in mlx-lm LoRA?
It multiplies the adapter output before adding it to the frozen weights, acting like alpha over rank in PEFT.
What happens if learning rate is too high?
Loss spikes or diverges as steps overshoot minima, sometimes corrupting the adapter beyond recovery.
What happens if learning rate is too low?
Training crawls; loss decreases slowly and the run ends undertrained within the iteration budget.
Why shuffle before splitting data?
To break any ordering in the source file so splits are identically distributed.
What is a deterministic split?
A split produced with a fixed seed so every run partitions the data identically.
What is the purpose of warmup steps?
They ramp the learning rate from zero so early updates on a fresh adapter do not destabilize training.
Why evaluate with batch size 1 on tiny test sets?
Evaluation batches cannot exceed the number of test examples, and batch 1 works at any size.
What is tokenization?
Splitting text into the subword units whose IDs the model actually consumes.
What does max_seq_length bound?
The token length of each training example; longer examples are truncated and memory scales with it.
What is an artifact store in ZenML?
The location where step outputs are serialized so later steps and runs can reuse them.
Why compare runs with a pinned seed?
It removes initialization and shuffling noise so metric differences reflect the hyperparameters.
What does mask_prompt exclude from the loss?
All prompt tokens, so gradients come only from the assistant's completion tokens.
What is a fused model directory?
A complete standalone model with adapter weights merged in, loadable without the original adapter files.
Why keep volumes/ out of git?
It holds service databases and artifacts that are machine-specific state, not source code.
What is drift between val and test scores?
Disagreement caused by tiny or unrepresentative splits; larger, well-mixed splits shrink it.
What makes a good smoke dataset?
Small enough to train in seconds but large and varied enough that split metrics are not pure noise.
